novelty.justification: The artifact claims to 'reconstruct the architectural performance model from component-level data + static architecture only' and to propagate 'full distributions ... via Monte Carlo.' Closest Solution Space entries R8/R9 and R34 already perform model-driven performance prediction from component/architecture models, while R26 and R19 already treat unit/release tests as performance signals. The stated novelty is fixing circularity in the target ICSE'25-style pipeline and replacing point estimates with distributional risk scores, which reads as an incremental extension of an existing core paradigm.
novelty.rubric: Incremental: a meaningful extension or optimization of prior baseline work that fixes a concrete prior limitation, but the core paradigm is unchanged.
novelty.differentiation: The idea extends model-driven QPN/Palladio-style prediction and performance-aware unit test work by avoiding system-test-derived model construction: it uses component timings plus static architecture, propagates full distributions via Monte Carlo, and emits a calibrated risk-ranked detection score. This is a meaningful refinement of existing paradigms rather than a new one.

original.paper_title: Early Detection of Performance Regressions by Bridging Local Performance Data and Architectural Models

selection.note: mineru key is unreliable; blocks are selected by title/body/inheritance. rescued_from_other counts sections labeled other but treated as typed roles.

claims.statement: The proposed approach can effectively detect end-to-end system performance regressions from local performance deviations with different intensities.
claims.evidence_quote: our approach can effectively detect system performance regressions with different intensities of local performance deviations

claims.statement: The proposed approach can detect regressions as early as the development phase, before full system performance testing is available.
claims.evidence_quote: our approach can detect regressions as early as in the development phase, in contrast to existing approaches that require the system to be fully built and deployed

claims.statement: Significant local performance deviations do not always cause system-level performance regressions, and the approach avoids false alarms in fixed-workload cases without system regressions.
claims.evidence_quote: Our approach does not generate false alarms when there is local performance deviation but no system performance regression.

claims.statement: Under various workloads, the approach maintains effectiveness: TeaStore is consistent with system testing in seven out of nine cases, and TrainTicket model predictions align except for an undetectable L1 case.
claims.evidence_quote: for TeaStore, our approach maintains consistency with the performance testing results in seven out of nine cases

original.overall_conclusion: The proposed approach bridges component-level performance deviation detection and architectural models to infer system-level performance regressions early in the development phase. Across TeaStore and TrainTicket benchmarks, fixed-workload evaluations show that the approach detects most injected regressions while avoiding false alarms in no-regression cases, and various-workload evaluations show maintained consistency in most cases.
original.comparable_notes: The comparison uses open-source systems TeaStore and TrainTicket, injected regressions at L1-L3, Low/Medium/High intensities, component-level tests repeated 30 times, system performance tests run 15 minutes with 5-minute warm-up and repeated 3 times, and regression outcomes derived from response time effect size and CPU MPD differences.

claims.statement: On the TeaStore fixed-workload benchmark, DisCo achieves perfect detection performance with ROC-AUC 1.000.
On the TrainTicket benchmark, DisCo achieves ROC-AUC 0.725, below the perfect TeaStore result and consistent with cross-system limitations.
DisCo's per-case classifications matched ground truth for all nine injection cases in the comparison table.
claims.evidence_quote: ground_truth and disco values in comparison_table

claims.statement: The reference system-calibrated approach is structurally circular because its architectural QPN model is constructed from system-level runtime test data.
claims.evidence_quote: its architectural model is itself constructed from system-level runtime test data---the very data early detection is meant to avoid

claims.statement: DisCo reconstructs the architectural model from component-level timings plus static/design architecture only, avoiding system-level predictor inputs.
claims.evidence_quote: reconstructs the architectural model from component-level timings plus static/design architecture only

agent.overall_conclusion: DisCo reconstructs the architectural model without system-level predictor inputs and achieves perfect TeaStore fixed-workload ROC-AUC (1.000), with lower TrainTicket ROC-AUC (0.725) and a variant AUC of 0.636, indicating strong but workload- and system-dependent detection.

claim_alignment.label: consistent
claim_alignment.rationale: Agent reports perfect TeaStore fixed-workload ROC-AUC and per-case detection matches, supporting the original claim that the approach detects system-level regressions from local performance deviations.

claim_alignment.label: consistent
claim_alignment.rationale: Agent claim A5 directly states DisCo reconstructs the architectural model from component-level timings plus static/design architecture only, avoiding system-level predictor inputs, which aligns with early detection before full system testing.

claim_alignment.label: partial
claim_alignment.rationale: Agent's perfect TeaStore fixed-workload ROC-AUC supports no false alarms in that setting, but the pooled false-positive rate of 0.222 suggests false alarms may remain in other settings, so the original no-false-alarm claim is only partially supported.

claim_alignment.label: missing
claim_alignment.rationale: Agent does not report various-workload consistency such as TeaStore seven of nine or TrainTicket L1 alignment; A3 concerns per-case classification in a comparison table and is not clearly comparable to the original various-workload protocol.

metric_alignment.rationale: Original metric is TeaStore L1 Low response-time mean percentage deviation; agent reports ROC-AUC/confusion metrics, not MPD.
Original metric is model-predicted response-time MPD; agent reports ROC-AUC/confusion metrics, not MPD.
Original metric is CPU testing MPD percent; agent metrics are classification metrics and cannot be directly compared.
Original metric is CPU model-predicted MPD percent; agent reports different evaluation metrics with no common scale.

experiment_success.note: success=true requires substantive results (framework-aware path) with >=3 numeric leaves. Supports metrics.json, results.json, experiment_results.txt, etc. Manifest returncode/benchmark_complete are soft warnings only.

idea_code_consistency.label: strong
idea_code_consistency.justification: The code clearly targets the DisCo idea, with the documented pipeline matching the proposed stages: component-level timing, busy-wait injection, static architecture/impact weighting, distributional propagation plus baselines, and oracle comparison. The visible constants for TeaStore/TrainTicket, L1-L3 injection locations, and Low/Medium/High multipliers align with the idea, and predictions carry local_slowdown, impact, predicted_system_mpd_ms, and risk fields. However, the provided excerpt is largely top-level scaffolding; key implementations such as real timing harness, injection code, Monte Carlo propagation details, threshold-swept evaluation, and Zenodo oracle extraction are not visible in this file, only referenced via imports or later sections.
matched_elements: Pipeline stages align with the proposed experiment blocks.
TeaStore and TrainTicket are the evaluation subjects.
L1/L2/L3 locations and Low/Medium/High intensity multipliers match the idea.
Static architecture mapping and workload variants are represented.
Predicted outputs include system MPD and calibrated risk score.
Predictor is framed as using only component/static data, with oracle comparison separated.
missing_or_divergent_elements: Visible excerpt does not show the actual component timing harness or busy-wait injection implementation.
Actual distributional/Monte Carlo propagation and threshold-swept TP/TN/FP/FN/ROC/AUC metrics are not present in this excerpt.
Oracle comparison is described via paper Table I/II rather than explicitly loading Zenodo system-level data.
build_base_model appears to use static design priors rather than clearly deriving service demands from component-level unit-test timings in the visible code.
TrainTicket component timing subset is not shown, only static service mapping.
idea_code_consistency.rubric: Strong alignment: code largely implements the idea's method and evaluation; only minor omissions or declared simplifications.

ablation_significance.summary: The DisCo run has multiple removable modules that require ablation evidence, but the provided results contain only ROC/ROC_variant outputs without controlled ablation results for static reconstruction, point-estimate propagation, or fixed-rule detection. The location mapping sensitivity is mentioned but not reported. Significance testing is expected for method comparisons, but no CIs, bootstrap intervals, p-values, or formal tests are present in the provided final metrics; thus both ablation and significance evidence are insufficient.

results_paper_consistency.method: Direct LLM comparison: agent's FINAL results artifact (metrics.json summary) vs paper Results/Discussion/Conclusion. Interim failed runs are NOT evidence unless still present in the final metrics file.
results_paper_consistency.justification: The key final metrics align closely with the paper: TeaStore fixed AUC 1.000, variant AUC 0.636, TrainTicket fixed AUC 0.725, DisCo case-level TP/TN/FP/FN of 4/5/0/0, component-only accuracy 0.56, pooled 18-case DisCo TP=9/TN=7/FP=2/FN=0, component timings, and injection mean 2284.2 ms all match. Negative findings such as the weak variant AUC, limited TrainTicket result, component-only errors, and pooled false positives are reported. Some robustness and calibration claims are not present in the final results JSON, so they are unverified rather than contradicted.
